source_identity.author: Eric Patterson
source_identity.title: Fantasy notes, analysis from Week 2 of NFL preseason

interpretation_policy.note: Source claims are historical evidence. Current fantasy truth requires fresh verification.

claims.source_claim: Smith completed all seven preseason attempts with a touchdown and connected twice with Adonai Mitchell; the article treats this as encouraging for the Jets passing offense and Garrett Wilson.
Warren started but Warren and Dowdle each received five carries, leaving the backfield without clear separation in this preseason sample.

claims.source_name_note: The pasted source text spells the player Jonathan Brooks; repository identity is Jonathon Brooks.
claims.source_claim: With Hubbard sidelined, Brooks started, handled five carries for 18 yards, scored on a goal-line touch, and also missed a routine pass-protection block. The article says he still has work to do to earn the starting job.
claims.interpretation: The start and goal-line touch are meaningful usage evidence, but Hubbard's absence prevents treating the role as won. Pass protection is an explicit downside recheck trigger.

claims.source_claim: Waddle caught a 35-yard pass on his first Broncos target and the article projects a path to lead Denver in receiving production.
Lloyd started for Green Bay and the article interprets this as evidence that he has earned the RB2 role, with contingent upside if Jacobs misses time.
Washington followed a 63-yard preseason opener with another explosive performance, including a 33-yard run, while Jeanty remains the clear starter.
Higgins' season-ending ACL injury opens the Texans WR2 competition; Noel and Dell remain injured, Hutchinson filled the role in this game, and the article suggests Collins may absorb more targets.

Tucker did not play while Nailor, Bech, and Benson did; the article interprets the pattern as evidence that Las Vegas views Tucker as its top wide receiver, while Bowers remains the primary receiving option overall.
claims.interpretation: Useful indirect hierarchy evidence, but not sufficient by itself to prove season-long WR1 routes or target volume.

claims.source_claim: Mendoza threw a pick-six and completed 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards in a step back from his preseason debut.
Black started and handled eight carries for 33 yards; the article interprets him as McCaffrey's direct backup with large contingent upside if McCaffrey misses time.
claims.interpretation: Meaningful for Black's roster-security evaluation; should be confirmed against broader current depth-chart and usage evidence before reclassification.

claims.source_claim: Stribling caught four of five targets for 46 yards after 63 yards in Week 1, with three Week-2 receptions delivered by Purdy; the article says he appears heavily involved despite not starting.
claims.interpretation: Repeated preseason production plus Purdy involvement is stronger than box score alone and supports the existing strong-hold thesis.

claims.source_claim: Hampton, Mitchell, and Vidal combined for eight carries and five yards in the first half, but the article explicitly warns against overreacting because the Chargers did not start their full offensive line and Herbert played only three snaps.
claims.interpretation: No downgrade to Keaton Mitchell's watch status from this result alone.
